Write a reproducible R script for one DietView analysis

Source: R/dv_script.R
dv_script.Rd

Turns the choices behind a view (predator, currency, reporting resolution, stratifying covariates and table rank) into a plain R script that rebuilds it with exported DietView functions only. The Shiny application (run_dietview()) uses it for its "Reproduce" tab, so a figure explored interactively can be archived and rerun without the application.

Usage

dv_script(
  prep,
  predator = NULL,
  mode = c("occurrence", "weight", "count"),
  currency = c("records", "numbers"),
  aggregation = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  rank = NULL,
  na_strata = c("drop", "show"),
  data_file = "dietview_prep.rds",
  file = NULL
)

Arguments

prep

A dietview_prep from dv_prepare().

predator

A predator to keep, or NULL (default) for all predators.

mode

What sizes the wedges: "occurrence" (prey records, or individuals with currency = "numbers"), "weight" or "count" (distinct prey items). See dv_sunburst().

currency

"records" or "numbers". See dv_tree().

aggregation

NULL (default: the full hierarchy, every record at every rank) or a list with threshold and, optionally, scope and min_predators, passed to dv_aggregate_threshold().

facet

Up to two covariates to draw one panel per level (or per combination of levels), or NULL. With two, c(inner, outer) as in the app: panels is then a list over the levels of outer, each a list over the levels of inner.

rank

Rank for the rank table and the frequency-of-occurrence table, by column name or display label, case-insensitive. Defaults to the third rank of prep.

na_strata

"drop" (default) leaves records with a missing covariate value out of the panels; "show" gives them an "NA" panel. As in run_dietview() and dv_build_html().

data_file

File name the script reads prep from.

file

Optional path; if given, the script is written there.

Value

A character vector of script lines, of class dietview_script (invisibly when file is given).

Details

The script starts from the prepared data saved with saveRDS(prep, data_file), so it does not depend on the network or on the state of WoRMS. Its header records the DietView and R versions, the date, the taxonomy source (with the worrms version and retrieval date when the lineage came from WoRMS) and the column specification.

Examples

prep <- dv_prepare(
  ices_diet[ices_diet$predator_common == "Atlantic cod", ],
  dv_spec(predator = "predator_common", stomach = "stomach_id",
          prey_id = "prey_aphia_id", prey_name = "prey_name",
          weight = "prey_weight_g", covariates = "quarter"),
  taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage, verbose = FALSE)
s <- dv_script(prep, mode = "weight",
               aggregation = list(threshold = 10, scope = "pooled"))
s
#> ## DietView analysis script
#> ## Generated 2026-11-03 00:36 UTC with DietView 0.1.0.9000 and R version 4.6.2 (2026-10-29).
#> ## Predator: all predators | wedges: weight | currency: records
#> ## Reporting resolution: threshold 10 stomachs, scope = pooled, min_predators = 1
#> # Taxonomy source: table
#> # Column specification of the prepared data:
#> #   predator = "predator_common"
#> #   stomach = "stomach_id"
#> #   prey_id = "prey_aphia_id"
#> #   prey_name = "prey_name"
#> #   weight = "prey_weight_g"
#> #   covariates = "quarter"
#> #   ranks = c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")
#> 
#> library(DietView)
#> 
#> ## 1. Prepared data (save it from R with saveRDS(prep, "dietview_prep.rds"))
#> prep <- readRDS("dietview_prep.rds")
#> spec <- prep$spec
#> prep
#> 
#> ## 2. Reporting resolution: rare prey merged up their lineage
#> ## (applied before selecting a predator, so pooled counts use all predators)
#> prep <- dv_aggregate_threshold(prep, threshold = 10, scope = "pooled", min_predators = 1)
#> attr(prep, "aggregation")
#> 
#> ## 3. Colors: one hue per phylum, from the pooled tree of all predators, so a
#> ## taxon keeps its color in every view (unidentified material is white)
#> pal <- dv_palette_tree(dv_build_tree(prep$data, prep$ranks))
#> 
#> ## 5. Multi-rank tree and sunburst

#> dv_sunburst(tree, mode = "weight", colors = pal, title = "All predators")
